newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to create four rapid-response formations.
newsitem.headline: Russia to create four rapid-response formations.

text.p: Russia plans to set up four rapid-response units next year, combining air, land and sea forces as part of large-scale military reforms, Defence Minister Igor Sergeyev said on Wednesday.

Sergeyev, quoted by Interfax news agency, told a meeting of decorated veterans that two "units of the future" would be set up in the Moscow military district, one in the Far East and one in the turbulent North Caucasus.
The agency quoted military experts explaining that Sergeyev's remarks meant the creation of rapid-response mobile formations with their own air and naval support.
It was not clear how large these might be.

The move would be in line with government plans to transform the underfunded and increasingly dilapidated 1.8 million-strong armed forces from an instrument of global warfare into a flexible fast-moving corps able to deal with regional conflicts.
Sergeyev, who was appointed last month, urged a quick start to thorough military reform. His predecessor was sacked for failing to move faster on reform.
"Time is the main factor," he said, adding that his concept of the reform had been provisionally approved by President Boris Yeltsin and Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.
RIA news agency, however, quoted Sergeyev as saying that the concept was still on the drawing board due to a lack of money.
President Boris Yeltsin has ordered Sergeyev to slash military expenditure to 3.5 percent of gross domestic product by the year 2000 from five percent now.

Sergeyev said he hoped to preserve combat-ready units with their infrastructures, but aimed to eliminate inefficient maintainance of the armed forces in general, and to make the military industry focus on modern technologies.
He expected a massive armaments and technical overhaul to be carried out between 2001 and 2005.
